baseObservation.meaning: immutable preimage observation only; Git owns live facts

claimBoundary: This contract makes current semantic ownership, contributor task routing and repository evidence freshness machine-checkable. It creates no business write authority, no global UI resolver, no provider/deployment/human assurance claim and no new serial convergence slice.

freshness.rule: A repository closure receipt is fresh only while every declared semantic input digest and every declared dependency receipt digest remains unchanged.
freshness.headBindingRule: Exact-head evidence is still required for PR acceptance; semantic input digests avoid invalidating unrelated closures for unrelated file changes.

observedMain.meaning: immutable rebase observation for contributor-runtime falsification; Git remains live-fact authority

contributorDoD.claimBoundary: Repository contributor routing, branch-policy discoverability and failure reproducibility only. It is not a human contributor study, review segregation proof, branch protection or deployment assurance.

repositoryCoherenceDebt.name: Repository Semantic Coherence Debt
repositoryCoherenceDebt.definition: Known drift or ambiguity between declared current authorities, current prose/API projections, repository-governance evidence and executable owners. A D-RSC finding does not automatically imply a current business-runtime defect.

closurePolicy.repositoryInternal: Close only when the stale projection/cause is retired or aligned at its actual owner and a falsifier proves the known failure family no longer reproduces.
closurePolicy.externalEvidence: Keep linked E3/E4 findings external; repository CI may route and observe them but may not self-close them.
closurePolicy.evidenceLimitation: Do not promote a skipped, conditional or unavailable evidence source to passed evidence; absence of that supplemental evidence is not automatically a failure of a different required rail.

findings.falsifier: Current authority topology no longer routes an engineer to the legacy app/server/lib rail as current authority, while retained legacy artifacts are explicitly classified as lineage/compatibility.
findings.limitation: Legacy files may remain for archaeology or compatibility; their presence alone is not a current runtime defect.
findings.candidateRemediation: ATLAS-1 authority-map legacy classification + current replacement routing

findings.falsifier: Current authoritative prose agrees with the executable UI owner on Home priority bound and Process Hub row/list geometry.
findings.limitation: A fresh document digest proves unchanged bytes, not agreement with executable UI semantics.
findings.candidateRemediation: ATLAS-1 README/START_HERE alignment with executable UI owner

findings.falsifier: OpenAPI describes the current Suite 3.0 runtime authority while preserving Suite 2.2 only as deprecated generator/implementation lineage.
findings.limitation: HTTP method/path parity alone does not establish semantic freshness of API descriptions.

findings.falsifier: Trajectory-sensitive PR declarations are checked against the actual diff or corrected before merge; a claim that convergence authority/workbook move together cannot survive when neither file is changed.
findings.limitation: The historical mismatch does not by itself prove the current convergence planning state is wrong.
findings.mitigation: PR template + DEVELOPMENT diff/declaration invariant; historical PR #146 remains immutable evidence

findings.falsifier: Observed GitHub settings protect main with the intended preventive rules/review enforcement and evidence is independently attributable.
findings.limitation: GOV-01F is compensating exact-SHA/provenance evidence; repository files cannot create or self-certify server-side prevention.

findings.falsifier: CodeQL may be counted only when the exact SHA has a completed successful CodeQL check; skipped remains not executed. Required first-party security rails are evaluated independently.
findings.limitation: Conditional CodeQL is supplemental; its absence must not be laundered into either a CodeQL pass or an automatic failure of the first-party required rails.

findings.falsifier: Legacy-only tools/literals are retired, relocated or explicitly classified so isolated reading cannot mistake them for the current runtime contract.
findings.limitation: Known legacy literals that are overwritten by the current bootstrap are lineage debt, not evidence of current runtime output.

findings.falsifier: Declared cross-owner semantic consistency predicates detect known drift families in addition to digest freshness; new drift families extend the vocabulary rather than being hidden by fresh receipts.
findings.limitation: Fresh means unchanged against a receipt; it does not mean globally semantically consistent with every other owner.
findings.mitigation: Documentation Runtime known cross-owner predicates + D-RSC mutation vocabulary; not a global semantic equivalence proof

negativeControls.statement: No second current business write authority was identified in the bounded current production-surface census.
No eighth business process was identified; EP-01 remains cross-cutting.
No AI path was identified that independently creates human business decisions.
No evident current quarantine bypass was identified in the audited repository paths.
No audited current cross-tenant selector was identified that bypasses membership binding.
No audited export path was identified that widens the actor read authorization.
No current standard-runtime path was identified that promotes the PostgreSQL benchmark substrate to production/deployment proof.
The seven procedure semantics remain distinct in the audited current contracts; completion, closure, mapping, rating and approval are not collapsed into stronger conclusions.

repositoryCoherenceDebt.claimBoundary: D-RSC is a repository-coherence debt projection and routing aid, not a second gap register, runtime authority, release gate or development roadmap. GAP-022 remains canonically owned by v3/gaps.json/E3-GOV. Negative controls are bounded observations, not formal proofs of absence.
